statement: This entry introduces partition DP, the pattern behind Matrix Chain Multiplication. The input is an array dimensions of length n + 1: matrix i, for 1 ≤ i ≤ n, is dimensions[i − 1] × dimensions[i]. Multiplying an a × b matrix by a b × c matrix costs a × b × c scalar multiplications.

Let f(i, j) be the cheapest cost of multiplying matrices i to j. A single matrix costs nothing, so f(i, i) = 0. Otherwise try every split point k with i ≤ k < j: multiply i..k, multiply k + 1..j, then join the two results for dimensions[i − 1] × dimensions[k] × dimensions[j].
f(i, j) is the smallest of those totals, and the answer is f(1, n), the smallest cost of multiplying the whole chain.

examples.explanation: The best split is in the middle, (A × B) × (C × D): 150 + 180 for the halves plus 5·3·5 = 75 to join them, 405 in total.
